rows.citation: Andrews, J. H., Briand, L. C., Labiche, Y. (2005). Is mutation an appropriate tool for testing experiments?. Proceedings of the 27th International Conference on Software Engineering (ICSE '05), 402.
rows.model_type: general software (programs with test pools and known real faults)
rows.controlled_mutations: yes - compares operator-generated mutants with real faults and hand-seeded faults as stand-ins in testing experiments.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - uses comprehensive test-case pools, but these are program inputs, not stimulation protocols.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - general programs; no signal or electrophysiology features.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - assesses fault realism, not test selection (per abstract).
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - abstract describes no discovery/held-out split.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Methodological support for mutants as proxies for real faults in software; NeuroSem would need domain evidence that NeuroML/LEMS mutants resemble real modelling faults.
rows.verification_method: Crossref api.crossref.org/works/10.1145/1062455.1062530 (authors, ICSE '05 proceedings, page 402, ACM Press); abstract from OpenAlex API; full text not openly available per OpenAlex/Semantic Scholar.
